title: got sick of public RPCs choking my bots, built a local C++ failover proxy. P99 tail is under 1ms under stress. Should I sell this or just keep it private?
author: Sad-Inflation-4049
selftext:
Hey guys,  
new to this group i run arbs strategy on prediction markets and got fed up with Alchemy/QuickNode throwing random 429s and latency spikes right during high volatility events. Standard cloud routers or retry scripts take like 2,3 seconds to recover, which completely kills the trade.

So I wrote a local C++ proxy that runs right next to the bot to hot-swap connections instantly. Kept it proprietary, but I just ran a brutal hardware stress test to see where it breaks. I synced 8 parallel worker threads to spam the proxy at the exact same microsecond to force maximum internal lock contention during a simulated crash.

The numbers:

 Proxy (Normal swap): 0.9ms to 1.9ms execution time.

 8-Thread stress test: Worst-case P99 tail latency clocked at 789 microseconds.

It basically reroutes the stream down a warm backup pipe before the bot even realizes the primary connection dropped.

I built this just to save my own prediction market arb strategy, but it's working so well I’m wondering if I should productize it. I'm thinking of either keeping it 100% private for my own operations, or offering it to solo quants/small syndicates or groups on a value-capture model (taking a small, capped cut of the mathematically proven alpha saved by the logs)or if you guys wanna suggest a model i’m all ears.

For anyone running live infra: Do serious funds actually pay for a plug and play, sub millisecond local failover layer, or do you guys just prefer to write your own internal wrappers?

Any reply is appreciated 👍🏼
